$comentario: The support panel (F3) and the subscription notices. It is translated like the rest of the POS even though one person uses it today: it is the same application, the same loose-text test guards it, and the day there is support staff in another country the work is done. Subscription states reuse the `company_status_*` keys from auth.json: same five words, and having them twice means having them differ.
$comentario_listado: RF-5. A customer's identity is the (affiliate, company) pair, so the table shows it as it is: «1·2» reads as a customer number and is what gets read out over the phone.
admin_companies_empty: There are no companies yet. Create the first one.
$comentario_uso: How much of what the plan allows is already in use. With an uncapped plan it does not say «0 of -1»: it says how many there are and nothing else.
$comentario_alta: RF-6. The affiliate and the company can be left blank: the backend takes the next free one, and computing it there keeps two simultaneous sign-ups from picking the same pair.
admin_new_intro: It is created with branch 001, register 00001, its settings and the first administrator.
admin_label_pair_hint: Blank: the next free one is used. Repeat the affiliate to open another company for the same customer.
admin_label_expires_hint: With the date blank, the subscription never expires and nobody gets a notice.
admin_label_document_locale_hint: The invoice is for the customer and for the tax authority: it need not be the language of whoever rings up the sale.
admin_created: {nombre} is now set up. Branch {sucursal}, register {caja}.
admin_created_pending: That email already had an account, so the membership stays pending until the person accepts it when signing in.
admin_texts_seeded: The receipt texts were seeded in {idioma}.
$comentario_ficha: A company's file: what you need to see to take a phone call, and the two things you can do —change the subscription and look inside—.
admin_no_admins: This company has no active administrator.
admin_subscription_derived: The stored status says «{guardado}» and the date has passed, so today it behaves as «{efectivo}».
admin_company_not_found: We could not find that company.
$comentario_entrar: RF-8 and RN-4. The reason is required, the visit lasts half an hour and it is read only. All three are stated on screen: whoever goes in has to know what they can do, and whoever audits has to be able to read why.
admin_enter_intro: For diagnosis. You will see the customer's data in read-only mode, the visit lasts {minutos} minutes and it is logged with your reason.
admin_enter_reason_hint: Whoever audits this in six months will read it: «check why the register will not close» works, «review» does not.
$comentario_bitacora: RF-9. It also keeps the customers' sign-ins, on purpose: the question that actually gets asked is not «what did support do» but «why can this cashier not sign in».
admin_audit_intro: Who did what, when, and to which company.
admin_audit_empty: No activity recorded with that filter.
$comentario_acciones: The names of the audit log actions. The key repeats the value the backend writes, so a new action is added here under the same name; until it is, the screen shows the raw code instead of a hole.
admin_action_login_soporte: Signed in to the support panel
$comentario_avisos: The subscription notices the customer sees in the POS (RF-11). The grace one and the read-only one are the ones that cost money, so they say what can still be done and not just what happened.
subscription_trial: You are on a trial period.
subscription_trial_until: You are on a trial period until {fecha}.

match.diasPlural=one: The payment is overdue. Today is the last day you can sell.
match.diasPlural=other: The payment is overdue. You can keep selling for {dias} more days.

subscription_read_only: The payment is overdue and the grace period is over. You can review your data and close the register, but not sell.
subscription_suspended: The subscription is suspended. Contact support to reactivate it.
subscription_contact: Contact support to settle the account.
$comentario_franja: The impersonation banner (RF-8). It is permanent and sits above everything on purpose: the worst thing that can happen on a support visit is forgetting that you are looking at someone else's company.
